cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith, who's staying on in Ephesus (1 Timothy 1:1-3). Paul just finished telling Timothy how people should act in God's household, the church (1 Timothy 3:14-15). Now Paul passes along something the Spirit expressly states about later times.

cards.question: The Spirit says that in later times, some people will do what?

cards.text: They walk away to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons. Paul says they're influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.
And Paul spells out what these people will tell everybody else not to do.

cards.question: These people will prohibit one thing and require abstinence from another. What are they?

cards.text: Friend, if somebody put a NO sign on my cookie jar, I'd climb right back in that junk drawer and pull a takeout menu over my head. But Paul says those foods aren't the problem, because God created them.

cards.question: Paul says God created these foods to be received with ___ by those who believe and know the truth.
Paul says some things God created should still be rejected, even when they're received with thanksgiving.
Paul says nothing received with thanksgiving should be rejected. What does he say sanctifies it?

answers.text: The word of God and prayer

cards.text: Paul tells Timothy to point these things out to the brothers. Timothy's been nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction he's followed.

cards.question: By pointing these things out to the brothers, Timothy will be a good ___ of Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Then Paul gets blunt: reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, Timothy's got some training to do.

cards.question: Instead of irreverent, silly myths, Paul tells Timothy to train himself for ___.

cards.text: Paul says physical exercise is of limited value. Limited, friend, not none, which is GREAT news, because my whole workout is hopping my gold base from the oven to the cooling rack.

cards.question: Paul says godliness is valuable in every way. Why?

answers.text: It holds promise for this life and the next
It keeps the body strong for longer
It earns respect from the elders

cards.text: Paul calls this a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance. Then he says this is exactly what they labor and strive for.

cards.question: Paul says they labor and strive because they've set their hope on the living God.

cards.text: And that living God? Paul calls Him the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
Command and teach these things, Paul tells Timothy. Then he gets personal about Timothy himself.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy not to let anyone despise something about him. What is it?
Paul tells Timothy to wait until he's older before he sets an example for the believers.

cards.text: In speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity: FIVE places to set the example. Friend, I've only got six topping jars and I STILL can't keep the sprinkles out of the peppermint.
And until Paul gets there, he wants Timothy devoted to three things.

cards.question: Until Paul comes, Timothy should devote himself to the public reading of ___, to exhortation and to teaching.

cards.text: Then Paul tells him not to neglect the gift that's in him. Friend, I KNOW neglected: I spent years in a junk drawer under a takeout menu.

cards.question: How was this gift given to Timothy?

answers.text: Through a prophecy as the elders laid hands on him
Through a dream from an angel of the Lord
Through a letter from the apostles in Jerusalem

cards.text: Be diligent in these matters, Paul says, and absorbed in them. ALL in, friend, no snooze button.

cards.question: If Timothy stays diligent and absorbed in these matters, his ___ will be evident to all.
Paul tells Timothy to pay close attention to his teaching, but says his own life matters less.

cards.text: Life AND teaching, friend, both of them. Then Paul tells Timothy to persevere in these things, because something big comes from it.

cards.question: If Timothy perseveres in these things, who does Paul say he will save?

answers.text: Both himself and those who hear him
Only the people who hear him
Only the elders who sent him

findings.problem: The question opens with "These people," which points back to cards 3 and 4. Those cards are no longer on screen, so the question never says who they are: the ones who abandon the faith in later times.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card says the foods aren't the problem "because God created them." That reasoning comes from 4:4 ("For every creation of God is good"), but the card cites only 1 Timothy 4:3.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card says the foods aren't the problem because God created them. That gives away card 8, which asks whether some things God created should still be rejected when received with thanksgiving (answer: False).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card says "Paul tells Timothy to point these things out to the brothers." In 4:6 this is not a command. Paul says that by pointing these things out, Timothy will be a good servant.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says this is what "they" labor and strive for. In 4:10 it is "we," which includes Paul. Card 17 repeats "they labor and strive because they've set their hope," which also leaves Paul out of his own statement.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke's logic doesn't hold. "Only six topping jars" is set against five places to set an example, but six is more than five, so "only" makes no sense. Keeping toppings from mixing also isn't the same action as setting an example across several areas of life.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The question asks "How was this gift given to Timothy?" The phrase "this gift" points back to card 7, which is no longer on screen. The question should say which gift: the gift that is in Timothy, which Paul tells him not to neglect.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. Both wrong answers start with "Only," and the right one starts with "Both." Card 12 also just stressed "Life AND teaching, friend, both of them," which points the baker to "Both" by pattern rather than by reasoning.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
